newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Yilmaz seeks right-wing alliance.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Yilmaz seeks right-wing alliance.

text.p: Turkey's prime minister-designate Mesut Yilmaz has called for a rightist alliance to keep the embattled Islamists out of power, but blamed his bitter rival Tansu Ciller for blocking such a move.

Speaking on television late on Friday, Yilmaz called for an alliance with Ciller's conservative True Path Party in his bid to forge a secularist coalition excluding the outgoing Islamist leader Necmettin Erbakan.
"The True Path Party is the easiest one with which we can form a partnership, make an election alliance and unite..," Yilmaz said in an interview on the private ATV channel.

"The only obstacle to this is the negative attitude of Tansu Ciller to me for personal reasons," he said from the garden of his Ankara residence, hours after President Suleyman Demirel handed him the mandate to form a Turkey's 55th government.
A meeting of Yilmaz's conservative Motherland Party was set for 11 a.m. (0800 GMT) in the first stage of what he said would be a short campaign to form a government.

He has vowed to present a government list by June 30 from among a host of squabbling leaders. He was to meet party leaders, including Ciller, on Tuesday for talks on forming a coalition aimed at taking the country to spring elections.

Yilmaz's Motherland Party has just 129 MPs in the 550-seat parliament. Two leftist parties have said they were prepared to back him, but he would still require substantial defections from the True Path Party.

Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, resigned on Wednesday under pressure from the secularist establishment. He attacked Demirel's decision to appoint Yilmaz rather than accept the Islamist leader's plans for a caretaker government.
"The president's behaviour was extremely wrong," Erbakan said at an official dinner on Friday evening.

Demirel, a veteran of political in-fighting, rejected a plan for a Ciller-led coalition and instead followed tradition by choosing Yilmaz as leader of the second-biggest faction in parliament after Erbakan himself.
